summary: Dedicated pool throughput sag from telemetry-sidecar prefetch saturation and slot fencing
description: Issue summary: BrightFlow reported a sustained throughput degradation in their dedicated eu-west pool during a midday window. Impact: customer p99 latency increased ~3x and several batched routes fell back to lower-concurrency variants; some requests returned 429s. Environment: Dedicated pool (eu-west), pinned to redwood-13b-v2. Symptoms appeared at 11:35 UTC and persisted ~45 minutes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer traffic pattern: many small, long-lived short-streams (avg payload 200 tokens) between 11:20-12:00 UTC
2) Trigger reproduction: run synthetic small-stream generator targeting customer-dedicated-pool with ~800 concurrent connections to simulate their fanned-out chatlets
3) Observe allocator/gpu metrics and autoscaler activity (slo, attach times, slot_count)
4) Reproduce logs: tail sidecar telemetry agent logs on nodes serving the dedicated pool
logs: [2026-03-12T11:36:12Z] allocator WARN: slot_fence_acquired tenant=bf-tenant lease_time_ms=120000 pinned=true
investigation_notes: 11:40 - Initial triage by CS: observed p99 jump and 429s; customer reports batching throughput halved for model redwood-13b-v2
11:48 - SRE fetched node allocation: several nodes in dedicated pool had >250 active prefetch leases from telemetry-sidecar process; KV-cache warmups stalled
11:55 - Heap of small short-streams visible in metrics; batcher queue length increased while GPU attach rate decreased; autoscaler skipped scale due to delayed telemetry metrics window

12:05 - Hypothesis: telemetry-sidecar ingestion (metrics/trace exporter) is aggressively prefetching model context and holding prefetch leases, causing slot fencing and reducing available GPU credits per node. Autoscaler sees stale metrics and defers scaling, so capacity not added in time.
12:18 - Runbooks checked: prefetch lease TTL normally 30s, observed >2m on some nodes due to sidecar retries under IO pressure

12:30 - Short-term mitigation applied: throttled sidecar telemetry ingestion and forced prefetch lease release on affected nodes; observed immediate drop in slot_fence_acquired events and gradual recovery of attach throughput
12:40 - Confirmed fallback behavior: routing policy moved some traffic to lower-concurrency variants to keep tail latency bounded while attachments recovered
comments: Support (Sasha Patel) 2026-03-12 11:42: We're seeing elevated p99 and some 429s for BrightFlow. Customer on dedicated tier, pinned model redwood-13b-v2. Collecting node and allocator traces.
SRE (Miguel Ortega) 2026-03-12 11:52: Found many long-lived prefetch leases held by telemetry-sidecar on 3 nodes. Openside: is the telemetry exporter retry loop causing lease retention?
CS (Alina Chen) 2026-03-12 12:00: Customer confirmed traffic is a burst of small chatlets from morning data pipeline. They observe degraded throughput but no request errors on their side.

SRE (Miguel Ortega) 2026-03-12 12:22: Applied throttle to telemetry collector (rate-limit exporter to 50 rps) and issued lease_release for affected nodes. Monitoring shows attach_throughput increasing.
Customer (BrightFlow Ops) 2026-03-12 12:35: Thanks — throughput returned to expected baseline over ~10 minutes. Please advise on permanent fix.

Support (Sasha Patel) 2026-03-12 12:50: Creating follow-ups: autoscaler metric-window tuning, sidecar backpressure control, and prefetch TTL guard for dedicated pools. Linking infra PR to patch exporter behavior.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: throttled telemetry exporter on affected nodes and force-released stale prefetch leases; autoscaler settings adjusted to use shorter metric windows for dedicated pools in high-fanout scenarios. Follow-ups: PR #4321 to add backpressure and exponential backoff in telemetry-sidecar (pending), implement prefetch lease hard-ttl enforcement (ops work), and add a per-tenant prefetch cap to prevent noisy tenants from monopolizing prefetch slots.
